title: Tenant latency-mediated interrupt and fairness protocol for continuous batching
creator: Priya Nair
description: Introduce a tenant-level interrupt and fairness protocol that mediates batching admission based on observed latency budgets and key-value cache residency. The goal is to reduce SLO breaches for latency-sensitive tenants while keeping overall GPU throughput high and avoiding thrashing the key-value cache. This ticket designs the algorithm, implements the admission controller and interrupt hooks in the runtime, and wires up observability and rollout controls in the console.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime implements a latency-mediated admission controller that can mark incoming requests as: allow, defer (short window), or interrupt (yield GPU slice)
Controller uses tenant-configured latency budget and a global GPU memory signal to decide actions; defaults are safe for existing workloads
Key-value cache residency heuristics are used to prefer deferring non-hot requests instead of interrupting hot working sets
End-to-end integration tests validate no increased p95 latency for high-priority tenants after rollout under synthetic mixed workloads
Console exposes a per-tenant ‘interrupts/sec’, cache-eviction, and SLO-breach trend; can toggle the new policy per deployment for canary
Performance benchmarks show throughput delta <= 6% for standard mixed workloads compared to baseline under similar SLOs
design_notes: We treat the key-value (KV) cache residency as a first-class signal: items with high residency score (hotset) get interrupt-resistant treatment
Policy is tenant-local and global-aware: local tenant latency posture is primary; a global GPU memory pressure gate can force more aggressive yielding when overall memory headroom is low
Prefer short deferral windows (10-50ms) for medium-latency tenants to allow batch completion without evicting large KV pages
Avoid full-service preemption unless a tenant is in immediate danger of SLO breach; instead use proportional throttles that slightly reduce batching window for lower-priority tenants
Algorithm should be deterministic given the same inputs to simplify repro and testing; stochastic backoff only introduced for tie-breaking to avoid synchronized oscillation
proposed_algorithm: 1) For each incoming request, compute a tenant latency deficit = (observed_p95 - tenant_p95_target) normalized by target. 2) Compute KV hotness penalty: hotness = weighted residency_score of keys touched by request. 3) Combine signals into an urgency score = alpha * latency_deficit + beta * (1 - hotness) + gamma * global_memory_pressure. 4) Map urgency to action: urgency < low_threshold -> allow; between low and high -> short defer window (10-50ms) and mark for opportunistic batching; > high_threshold -> interrupt (yield slice / move to low-priority lane) and optionally extend future soft-quota reductions. 5) Update tenant credit ledger to ensure fairness over time; credits replenish at tenant_rate configured by SLA tier.
memory_model: Maintain a sliding GPU memory horizon metric aggregated per GPU host: instant_used, kv_resident_bytes_by_tenant, estimated_eviction_cost. Use eviction_cost/time-to-warm to bias decisions away from evicting hot KV pages. When estimated_eviction_cost exceeds a threshold we favor deferral over interrupt for requests that would touch hot pages.
testing_plan: Unit tests for urgency calculation with synthetic residency and latency inputs
Integration tests that simulate mixed tenants (latency-sensitive, throughput-heavy, cold-batch) and assert SLOs and fairness quotas
Chaos tests that flip global_memory_pressure to validate policy stability and lack of oscillation
Long-running soak (48h) with production-like traces to measure KV churn and throughput delta
Load test comparing before/after policy using our existing benchmark harness (link below)
rollout_plan: Feature flag gated in runtime; default off
Canary: enable on a single dedicated pool with low-risk tenants for 24h, monitor costs and SLOs
Gradual ramp: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% of pools over 2 weeks with checkpoints at each step
Console toggle to revert per-pool immediately; automated rollback if SLO breaches spike above threshold
Post-rollout: 2-week observation window and follow-ups for tuning alpha/beta/gamma
risks: Mis-tuning alpha/beta/gamma could oscillate and cause global throughput degradation
Estimating key hotness requires recent access telemetry; stale signals could bias decisions incorrectly
Increased complexity in runtime decision path could add small CPU overhead; need to ensure overhead < 1% of request CPU time
Edge-case workloads that touch extremely large working sets may still suffer eviction churn despite deferral heuristics
notes: Follow-ups: expose tenant credit replenishment config in console; add a small ML model to predict eviction cost from recent access patterns
Consider a lightweight on-GPU estimator for residency to reduce host<->agent round trips in a future iteration
Coordinate with SRE for alert thresholds and automated mitigations during rollout
